amendments.rule: Expect more fusion rather than new rules: *Nor* for waw plus a negative, *But* for `כִּי אִם`, *whatsoever* for `כֹּל אֲשֶׁר`. The same *Nor* may rest on a present negative in one line and a gapped one in the next; align what is actually there. **Distance does not break these fusions.** Where the ASV's single word still says what every morpheme in it says, the unit stands however far apart they stand: `וְ ... לֹא` → *Nor* across a fronted prepositional phrase or object, `לֹא ... לְעוֹלָם` → *never* across the verb it negates. This is the far side of rule 30's contiguity condition, and the difference is what the English word carries. `גָּדַל ... מִן` → *exceeded* drops the preposition's own sense, so rule 2 splits it and the preposition is `unrepresented`; *Nor* still carries both the coordination and the negation and *never* both the negation and the time, so nothing is left over to mark. Head a *Nor* on the negative, which is what distinguishes it from a bare *and*. A *never* is a genuine tie between the negative and the temporal noun — the corpus heads it both ways — so choose, and say in the note which reading you took and that the corpus heads it both ways. **A single negative word written for a negative and a universal or indefinite quantifier standing in the same clause is one of these fusions.** Where Hebrew writes `כָל` on the noun, or an indefinite such as `מְאוּמָה` in the clause, and `לֹא`, or a prohibitive `אַל`, on its verb, and the ASV spends one word on the pair — `כָל־אָדָם לֹא־יִהְיֶה` → *there shall be* ***no*** *man*, `וְכָל־מְלָאכָה לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ` → *shall do* ***no*** *manner of work*, `לֹא־יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה` → *there shall cleave* ***nought*** *to thy hand* — that word carries both the quantification and the negation, exactly as *whatsoever* carries both morphemes of `כֹּל אֲשֶׁר`, so the two share one unit, discontinuous around the noun and the verb under rule 25, and headed on the negative for the reason a *Nor* is: the negation is what distinguishes *no* from *all* and *nought* from *aught*. Do not read rule 15's determiner sentences as a direction to give the word to one of them and mark the other `unrepresented`; that rule counts one determiner against one morpheme, and here one English word answers to two. **But read whether the quantifier keeps an English word of its own before fusing.** What rule 15 governs is a quantifier the ASV still writes — a `כֹּל` rendered *any* or *all* beside a *no* or a *not* elsewhere — and what this sentence governs is one where the single negative word is the whole of what both morphemes are rendered by. The noun the quantifier stands on keeps its own English either way, including any generic the ASV supplies to expand it under rule 31, so *manner of work* is `מְלָאכָה`'s, headed on *work*, and the `מִן־הַחֵרֶם` of the `מְאוּמָה` clause above keeps its own *of the devoted thing*. Where the ASV instead writes a word for each — a *not* on the verb beside an *any* or an *all* on the noun — nothing is indivisible, rule 2 splits them, and each morpheme takes the word written for it. **A *cannot* is not one of these fusions, because the verb's lexeme stands outside it.** Where the ASV writes *cannot* for a negated verb, the word carries the negation together with a modal English has supplied, and it goes whole to the negative while the verb keeps its subject pronoun and its lexical verb under rule 17: `לֹא יִצְעָדוּ` → *they* ***cannot*** *go* gives *cannot* to `לֹא` and *they go* to the verb, exactly as rule 48 gives such a word to the privative `מִן` that carries the negation there. The corpus aligns `לֹא` alone to *cannot*, headed on it, in fourteen units. **But where `יָכֹל` stands in the clause, that verb is what the modal renders**, and the two morphemes share the one indivisible word — `לֹא אוּכַל` → *I cannot*, `לֹא יוּכְלוּ` → *they cannot*, `לֹא נוּכַל` → *we cannot* — headed on *cannot*, which is how the corpus reads all eleven of those units. And where the ASV writes the negation and the modal as two words instead — *are not able*, *shall not be able* — nothing is indivisible, rule 2 splits them, the negative takes only its own *not*, and the rest belongs to the verb, its complement headed by rule 44. Read the English the ASV wrote and the verb the Hebrew wrote, not the modality the Hebrew implies.
amendments.why: The fusion sentence named `כֹּל` alone, and DEU.13.17's `לֹא־יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה` → *there shall cleave nought* is the same construction with an indefinite pronoun: one English word carries the negation and the quantification, and neither morpheme owns a part of it. Read narrowly, the old sentence sent a verse pass back to rule 15's determiner sentences, which would give *nought* to `לֹא` and leave `מְאוּמָה` `unrepresented` — the outcome the sentence's own next clause forbids. The widening is carried by rule 30's one-rendering condition, which is fully general, and by the structural identity with the two `כֹּל` examples already in the rule; I also added the boundary the case exposed, that the quantifier must be left with no English of its own, so the widening cannot swallow rule 15's *not ... any* shape. No corpus row was queried for `מְאוּמָה`, so the example is this chapter's; the rule's other counts are left exactly as they stood.

conventions: In the Egypt formula, the מִן of מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם and מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים takes the whole *out of* and heads on *out* under rule 24, while the Hiphil participle of יָצָא or פָּדָה keeps only *brought* or *redeemed*. The competing reading, which takes *out* as the verb's phrasal particle under rule 44 and leaves *of* to the preposition, is rejected chapter-wide. DEU.13.5 (three occurrences) and DEU.13.10 (two).

An adverbial בְּ plus article plus substantive that the ASV renders by a single English adverb — בַּסֵּתֶר → *secretly*, בָּרִאשֹׁנָה → *first*, בָּאַחֲרֹנָה → *afterwards* — fuses the preposition with the substantive under rule 30, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme, while the separately segmented article, bracketed or not, stands outside the fusion and is `unrepresented`: the one English word carries the relation and the lexeme but not the definiteness, which is why rule 30 does not absorb it. DEU.13.6, DEU.13.9 (twice).

שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל is divided by what the ASV writes for the preposition and not by the idiom. וּבְקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ → *and obey his voice* leaves the בְּ `unrepresented` under rule 40, the noun and suffix keeping their own English; כִּי תִשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהוָה → *when thou shalt hearken to the voice of Jehovah* gives it the written *to*. DEU.13.4 and DEU.13.18 are not a split, and the BSB disagreement on the first is a convention difference.

In the range מִקְצֵה הָאָרֶץ וְעַד־קְצֵה הָאָרֶץ → *from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth*, the whole *even unto* is the עַד's rendering under rule 16 and heads on *unto*, and the waw is `unrepresented`. Rule 26's waw-takes-the-connective shape does not arise, because the ASV writes no *and* here; and rule 14's bare *even* is not what was written, the corpus aligning a waw to *even unto* in no unit. The two supplied contrastive determiners *the one* and *the other* join their construct nouns under rule 15. DEU.13.7.

report: Read all 45 candidate lemma groups and the full 18-verse dump end to end. No cross-verse split found: patches is empty and no accepted edge was touched.

Demonstrative phrases are uniform. הַנָּבִיא הַהוּא and הַחֹלֵם הַהוּא (13.3, 13.5), הָעִיר הַהִיא (13.15) and הַתּוֹעֵבָה הַזֹּאת (13.14) each give the written determiner to the demonstrative pronoun and leave every article in the phrase unrepresented, the construct taking a supplied *the* where such a phrase is the nomen rectum (13.3 *the words of that prophet*, 13.15 *the inhabitants of that city*). That is rule 41's closing paragraph on שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא, applied identically four times.

מִן is aligned to the whole *out of*, headed on *out*, in all five Egypt/bondage occurrences (13.5 s024, s031, s037; 13.10 s022, s025), the Hiphil participles holding only *brought*. Heads on מוּת are uniformly on *death* (13.5, 13.9, 13.10), whether the ASV writes *shall be put to death*, *put to death*, or the compressed *to death* of וָמֵת.

Three apparent splits are licensed by what the ASV wrote and must not be reconciled away. שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל leaves בְּ unrepresented in 13.4 (*obey his voice*) and takes the written *to* in 13.18. בָּהּ fuses to *therein* in 13.15 but splits into *in* plus an unrepresented suffix in 13.5, where the ASV wrote *which ... to walk in* and no pronominal adverb — the two halves of rule 22. לְ before an infinitive takes a written *to* in 13.3, 5, 9, 10, 12 and 18, and is unrepresented in 13.11, where *shall do no more* writes no function word for it (rule 52's last sentence).

The candidate table is blind to `added`, so I read the dump for folded-versus-added asymmetry. All three `added` units are in 13.14 — *if*, the second *and*, and *that* — each a supplied connective over a clause with no conjunction in it (rules 55 and 14). Every supplied word folded into a neighbour elsewhere has a morpheme licensing it: *Certain* and *the one*/*the other* fall to their nouns under rule 15, *such ... as* to the comparative כְּ, *any* to the assimilated article of 13.11 under rule 41, and *tell* inside the verb's own rendering *hear tell*. No verse folds a clause subordinator into a waw or a הִנֵּה.

BSB: none of the 34 disagreements is a genuine error. They are the documented convention families — object markers (rule 16), articles for which the ASV writes no *the* (rules 29, 41, 47), the לְ of לֵאמֹר (rule 27), paragogic nun (rule 32), prepositions the ASV's recasting silences (rule 40), and a resumptive suffix rendered once (rule 22, 13.2 and 13.5). The two waws it flags are cases where the ASV writes no connective at all: 13.7, where the whole *even unto* belongs to the עַד under rule 16, and 13.10, where וָמֵת is compressed into *stone him to death*.

Recorded four conventions and one amendment. The amendment widens rule 35's fusion sentence, which names כֹּל alone, to cover DEU.13.17's לֹא ... מְאוּמָה → *nought*; left as written it invites a later pass to fall back on rule 15 and mark one of the two morphemes unrepresented, which rule 35 itself forbids.

Flagged for a later chapter, not promoted here: rule 50 covers אַיִן, אֶפֶס and Aramaic אִיתַי but has no sentence for the Hebrew positive existential יֵשׁ. DEU.13.3's הֲיִשְׁכֶם אֹהֲבִים → *whether ye love* was aligned by the exact analogue of rule 50's אִיתֵי כוֹן פָלְחִין → *ye serve* — particle unrepresented, suffix takes the subject pronoun — but on one occurrence with no corpus query for יֵשׁ that is too thin to promote.
